question: Which parts of sealed BA25 are externally known/equivalent, which are JANUS-specific integration, and what remains genuinely open before any general-SAT promotion?

external_literature.title: Algorithms for propositional model counting
external_literature.relevance: Explicit #SAT dynamic programming using primal, dual, and incidence tree decompositions; establishes that treewidth-based model counting is prior art.

external_literature.title: A Faster Algorithm for Propositional Model Counting Parameterized by Incidence Treewidth
external_literature.relevance: States #SAT is FPT for the width k of a given tree decomposition of the incidence graph; strengthens the external equivalence of BA25's bounded-width core.

external_literature.title: Constraint satisfaction with bounded treewidth revisited
external_literature.venue: Journal of Computer and System Sciences 76(2), 103-114
external_literature.relevance: Places primal, dual and incidence treewidth within the wider structural CSP/FPT tractability landscape.

external_literature.title: Knowledge Compilation, Width and Quantification
external_literature.relevance: Bounded-treewidth CNF can be transformed to deterministic DNNF; model counting and related operations fit a known knowledge-compilation width framework.

external_literature.title: Model Counting for CNF Formulas of Bounded Modular Treewidth
external_literature.relevance: Shows structural #SAT tractability extends beyond ordinary incidence treewidth; therefore low incidence width is one member of a broader known tractability family, not a unique general route.

external_literature.title: Compilation and Fast Model Counting beyond CNF
external_literature.relevance: FPT compilation/model counting for conjunctions of certain constraints parameterized by incidence treewidth, explicitly subsuming the known CNF result.

external_literature.title: A c^k n 5-Approximation Algorithm for Treewidth
external_literature.relevance: In 2^O(k)n time either proves tw>k or returns a decomposition of width at most 5k+4; demonstrates that a supplied decomposition need not be obtained by an unverified heuristic.

external_literature.author: Tuukka Korhonen
external_literature.title: A Single-Exponential Time 2-Approximation Algorithm for Treewidth
external_literature.relevance: In 2^O(k)n time either proves tw>k or outputs width at most 2k+1; important for composing any future logarithmic-width residual theorem with a certified decomposition route.

bounded_incidence_or_factor_treewidth_SA.finding: The general principle that SAT is tractable/FPT on bounded treewidth decompositions is established prior art.

bounded_incidence_treewidth_exact_model_.finding: Exact #SAT parameterized by a given incidence-treewidth decomposition is established prior art.

BA25_arbitrary_CNF_semantic_embedding.finding: The embedding calibrates expressiveness and width; it does not bound the width of arbitrary CNF.

BA25_tau_embedding_relation.finding: Adding singleton block leaves and the independent fresh-z path preserves the original incidence graph as a subgraph and changes width only by the frozen max(1,.) convention.

components: special DBO + arbitrary foreign-CNF factorization with explicit block/clause/variable node roles
one-bit local summaries plus global DBO witness state under the frozen PC_HYBRID_FACTOR_TD_V1 certificate grammar
proof-carrying SAT/#SAT/witness replay with per-bag/transition receipts
sealed BA20/BA21 source-return linkage where applicable
explicit no-materialization firewalls preserving BA23 lessons
JANUS_specific_contribution_candidate.promotion_rule: Do not call these components mathematically novel without a dedicated exact prior-art search for the same representation/certificate schema.

non_equivalences_and_firewalls: BA25 bounded-tau FPT != general polynomial SAT
arbitrary-CNF semantic embedding != bounded tau for arbitrary CNF
arbitrary-CNF semantic embedding != arbitrary foreign-CNF BA4 carrier transport
supplied/verified tree decomposition != proof that an optimal decomposition is cheaply available
FPT in tau != polynomial when tau is unbounded

decomposition_acquisition_implication.finding: If a future fixed exact reducer proves tau(REDUCE(F))=O(log |F|), then known 2^O(k)n constant-factor treewidth-approximation algorithms are compatible in principle with a polynomial composed route: a constant-factor O(log n) decomposition still gives BA25 runtime 2^O(log n)*poly(n).
decomposition_acquisition_implication.important_limit: This is only a conditional composition observation. BA25 itself proves no logarithmic residual-width bound and no universal reducer theorem.

audit_verdict.primary_next_question: Can one fixed cheap exact reduction force every SAT residual to O(log n) verified width or into a fixed audited tractable terminal class?

master_hypotheses.H2: REDUCE(F) belongs to LOW_WIDTH or a fixed finite union of audited polynomial tractable classes
master_hypotheses.H3: EXISTS F_n with tau(REDUCE(F_n))=Omega(n^alpha) while residuals evade every audited tractable terminal
